name: Despair

counsel.text: Now, if hereby thou dost not find success to a conquest, yet thou wilt be staid in the chariot, that thou shalt not fly out of the field until the battle be ended; thou wilt be kept from an utter despondency and a lying down under thy unbelief, or a turning aside to false means and remedies, that in the issue will not relieve thee.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

counsel.text: Though it may seem somewhat long to thee, whilst thou art under thy trouble and perplexity, yet it shall surely come in the appointed time of the Lord Jesus; which is the best season.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

counsel.text: What a fool, quoth he, am I, thus to lie in a stinking dungeon, when I may as well walk at liberty! I have a key in my bosom, called Promise, that will, I am persuaded, open any lock in Doubting Castle.
counsel.author: John Bunyan
counsel.source: The Pilgrim's Progress, Part 1, Doubting Castle

counsel.text: But, oh, how good a thing it is for God to send His word! For about a fortnight before I was looking on this very place, and then I thought it could not come near my soul with comfort, therefore I threw down my book in a pet. Then I thought it was not large enough for me; no, not large enough; but now, it was as if it had arms of grace so wide that it could not only enclose me, but many more besides.
counsel.author: John Bunyan
counsel.source: Grace Abounding to the Chief of Sinners, §204

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.text: God of all comfort and Father of mercies, you are near to the brokenhearted, and you do not despise a broken and contrite heart. I come only in the name of your Son. I confess that I have given up hope in your mercy. I have believed the voice that says I am beyond saving, and I have trusted my feelings more than your promises. I have thought my sin greater than the blood of Christ, and treated his promises as if they were for others and not for me. I have pulled away from prayer, from your Word, and from your people. This too is sin, and I bring it to you. Christ said that whoever comes to him he will never cast out. I come now, just as I am. He died for the ungodly, and he lives to intercede for me. For his sake forgive me. Holy Spirit, lift my head, and pour your love into my heart. Be my hope. I thank you that your mercies are new every morning, and that your faithfulness is great. In Jesus' name. Amen.

prayers.title: When everything looks dark
prayers.text: Lord, I cannot see the way out, and I am tired. I do not feel your nearness, but your Word says you are near. Hold on to me when I cannot hold on to you. Why are you cast down, O my soul? Hope in God. Keep me from the lie that nothing will ever change. Give me enough light for the next step and strength to take it, and bring a brother or sister to my side today. Lord Jesus, you were a man of sorrows and acquainted with grief, so I am not alone in this. Amen.

prayers.title: When I feel beyond hope
prayers.text: Father, I feel beyond your reach, but nothing in all creation can separate your children from your love in Christ Jesus. My feelings are not the final word; your promise is. I put my hope in you, not in how I feel. You are working in ways I cannot see. Help me to wait for you more than the watchman waits for the morning. Keep me close to your Word and your people until the light returns. I believe; help my unbelief. Amen.

examinationQuestions: When the darkness pressed in today, what did you believe about God: that he had forgotten you, or that he was able and willing to save?
Did you treat your feelings as the final word, above the promises of God?
Have you kept your sorrow to yourself instead of telling your pastor or a trusted believer?
Have you stopped praying, reading, or gathering with God's people because you thought it would do no good?
Which promise of Christ will you hold on to tomorrow, even if you do not feel it?
fleeActions: Say one promise of God out loud, such as John 6:37, and tell him you are holding him to it.
Do not stay alone with this. Call or message a brother or sister in your church right now and tell them how dark it is.
Get up, step outside if you can, and do one small ordinary task. Faith often moves one step at a time.
Write down what the voice of despair is telling you. Beside it, write what God says in his Word.
Send your pastor a message today and ask to talk. Seeing a doctor as well is wise, not faithless.
Read Psalm 42 aloud, and speak to your own soul as the psalmist did: hope in God.

afterFallReadings.text: And this I well remember still, that of all the sleights that Satan used to take this scripture from me, yet he never did so much as put this question, But do you come aright? And I have thought the reason was, because he thought I knew full well what coming aright was; for I saw that to come aright was to come as I was, a vile and ungodly sinner, and to cast myself at the feet of mercy, condemning myself for sin.
afterFallReadings.author: John Bunyan
afterFallReadings.source: Grace Abounding to the Chief of Sinners, §215

help.text: If you are thinking about ending your life, please call or text 988 now (in the US) or your local emergency number. Then tell your pastor or a trusted believer today. You are not a burden to them.
help.label: Call or text 988
